Illinois Fighting Illini.subtitle: Orange and Blue · Champaign–Urbana
Illinois Fighting Illini.history: Illinois athletics dates to the 19th century, and the university was a charter member of the Big Ten in 1896 and the NCAA in 1906. For men's basketball, the program's defining eras stretch from the undefeated 1915 team through the Whiz Kids, the Flyin' Illini, the 37-win 2005 team, and the return to the Final Four in 2026.
championships: Men's basketball: 1915 retroactive Helms national championship
Men's basketball: 6 NCAA Final Fours — 1949, 1951, 1952, 1989, 2005, 2026
Men's basketball: 18 Big Ten regular-season championships
Men's basketball: 4 Big Ten Tournament championships — 2003, 2005, 2021, 2024
Illinois athletics: 18 NCAA team championships and five recognized football national championships
lore: The 2004–05 team went 37–2, reached No. 1, and produced the famous comeback against Arizona in the Elite Eight before advancing to the national title game.
The 1988–89 'Flyin' Illini' reached the Final Four with a fast, athletic roster that became one of the program's defining teams.
Memorial Stadium's Red Grange legacy and the State Farm Center basketball tradition give Illinois two distinct home-field identities.
fun_facts: The 1915 basketball team finished 16–0 and 12–0 in conference play.
The 2005 team's 37 wins remain the most in program history.
Illinois returned to the Final Four in 2026 for the first time since 2005.

Kansas Jayhawks.subtitle: Rock Chalk · Lawrence
Kansas Jayhawks.history: Kansas basketball is tied directly to the origins of the sport: James Naismith coached at KU, and his successor Phog Allen became the program's foundational figure. Across generations led by Allen, Larry Brown, Roy Williams, and Bill Self, Kansas developed into one of college basketball's defining blue-blood programs.
championships: 6 recognized men's basketball national championships — 1922, 1923, 1952, 1988, 2008, 2022
4 NCAA Tournament championships — 1952, 1988, 2008, 2022
15 Final Four appearances through the 2026 NCAA Tournament
Bill Self led Kansas to two national championships and a record-tying run of 13 straight Big 12 regular-season titles from 2005–2017
lore: Allen Fieldhouse opened in 1955 and is named for Phog Allen, the 'Father of Basketball Coaching.'
The Rock Chalk chant is inseparable from Kansas basketball and Allen Fieldhouse's reputation as one of the sport's most intimidating home environments.
Kansas' coaching tree connects Naismith and Allen to a remarkable number of Hall of Fame figures, including Dean Smith and Adolph Rupp.
fun_facts: Phog Allen won 24 conference championships and three recognized national titles during his Kansas coaching career.
Four of Kansas' six recognized national championships came in the NCAA Tournament era.
Bill Self became Kansas' all-time winningest coach in 2024, passing Phog Allen.

Kansas City Chiefs.subtitle: Chiefs Kingdom · Kansas City
Kansas City Chiefs.history: Lamar Hunt founded the franchise as the Dallas Texans in the AFL before moving it to Kansas City in 1963. The Chiefs played in the first Super Bowl, won their first Super Bowl championship after the 1969 season, then returned to the sport's summit under Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes more than half a century later.
championships: 4 Super Bowl championships — IV, LIV, LVII, LVIII
AFL championship as the Dallas Texans in 1962, before the move to Kansas City
AFC championships following the 2019, 2020, 2022 and 2023 seasons
lore: The Lamar Hunt Trophy, awarded to the AFC champion, is named for the Chiefs founder and AFL architect.
Arrowhead became one of the NFL's defining home-field environments, with tailgating and crowd noise central to Chiefs culture.
The Reid–Mahomes era transformed a franchise known for decades of postseason heartbreak into the NFL's modern dynasty.
fun_facts: The Chiefs represented the AFL in Super Bowl I against Green Bay.
Super Bowl IV delivered the franchise's first Super Bowl title with a 23–7 win over Minnesota.
By winning Super Bowl LVIII, Kansas City became the second NFL team of the 21st century to repeat as Super Bowl champion.

St. Louis Cardinals.subtitle: The Birds on the Bat · St. Louis
St. Louis Cardinals.history: The Cardinals are one of baseball's most decorated franchises and have played in the National League since 1892. Their identity runs through generations of stars and eras — the Gas House Gang, Stan Musial, Bob Gibson and Lou Brock, Whiteyball, Mark McGwire, Albert Pujols, Yadier Molina and Adam Wainwright.
championships: 11 World Series championships
19 National League pennants
28 first-place finishes in National League play through the start of the 2026 season
lore: The 'Cardinal Way' became shorthand for the organization's emphasis on player development, fundamentals, continuity and winning expectations.
Branch Rickey helped pioneer the modern farm-system model while running the Cardinals, creating a structural advantage that shaped baseball far beyond St. Louis.
Stan Musial remains the franchise's statistical icon, while Bob Gibson's 1968 season became part of baseball mythology.
fun_facts: The 1942 Cardinals went 106–48 and erased a 10.5-game deficit on the way to a World Series championship.
Joe Medwick's 1937 Triple Crown remains the most recent by a National League hitter.
The Cardinals have won more World Series titles than any National League franchise.

Denver Nuggets.subtitle: Mile High Basketball · Denver
Denver Nuggets.history: Denver's pro basketball lineage began in the ABA before the Nuggets joined the NBA in the 1976 merger. The franchise developed distinctive eras around David Thompson, Alex English, Dikembe Mutombo, Carmelo Anthony and, ultimately, Nikola Jokić — whose teams finally broke through to the franchise's first NBA championship.
championships: 1 NBA championship — 2023
1 Western Conference championship — 2023
Multiple division championships across the NBA era
lore: The 1994 Nuggets became the first No. 8 seed in NBA history to defeat a No. 1 seed, stunning Seattle in a five-game first round.
The rainbow skyline uniforms became one of the NBA's most recognizable visual identities and remain central to Nuggets nostalgia.
Nikola Jokić turned Denver into a championship team with a style built around passing, spatial awareness and an offense run through a center.
fun_facts: The Nuggets' 2023 championship was the first NBA title in franchise history.
Alex English remains one of the signature scorers of the 1980s and the franchise's longtime points icon.
Denver joined the NBA in 1976 as part of the ABA–NBA merger.

Colorado Avalanche.subtitle: Go Avs Go · Colorado
Colorado Avalanche.history: The Avalanche arrived in Denver from Quebec in 1995 and immediately became champions, winning the Stanley Cup in their first Colorado season. The Sakic–Forsberg–Roy era established the franchise as an NHL power, and a new core led by Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar returned the Cup to Colorado in 2022.
championships: 3 Stanley Cup championships — 1996, 2001, 2022
Presidents' Trophy winners in 2001, 2021 and 2026
13 division titles in the franchise's first 30 Colorado seasons through 2025–26
lore: Colorado won the Stanley Cup in 1996, its very first season after relocating from Quebec — the first major professional championship for the city of Denver.
The late-1990s and early-2000s Avalanche–Red Wings rivalry became one of the fiercest rivalries of its NHL era.
Ray Bourque finally lifting the Stanley Cup after the 2001 championship is one of hockey's defining celebration images.
fun_facts: Joe Sakic won Stanley Cups with the organization as captain in 1996 and 2001 and as the executive architect of the 2022 champion.
The 2022 Avalanche went 16–4 in the postseason.
The franchise won nine consecutive division titles from 1995 through 2003.

Denver Summit FC.subtitle: Together We Climb · Denver
Denver Summit FC.history: Denver Summit FC is Colorado's first NWSL club and the league's 16th franchise. The club began play in 2026 after growing from a community-backed effort to bring top-flight professional women's soccer to Colorado, making its inaugural season a rare chance to watch a team's traditions form in real time.
championships: Expansion club — inaugural NWSL season in 2026
No championships yet; the club's competitive history is being written
lore: The Summit name was selected through a community vote that drew more than 15,000 fan votes and submissions.
The crest's main mountain peak is angled at 26 degrees as a nod to the club's 2026 debut, while green and white reference classic Colorado license plates.
The inaugural home match at Empower Field drew 63,004 fans, setting a new NWSL single-match attendance record.
fun_facts: The club's first home match was a 0–0 draw against the Washington Spirit on March 28, 2026.
Denver used three home venues during its inaugural season: Empower Field at Mile High, DICK'S Sporting Goods Park and Centennial Stadium.
The inaugural Evergreen Kit was revealed at Denver Union Station with the Colorado Symphony.
